hints: Use the Binomial Theorem to expand $\left(2 - \frac{3}{2}x\right)^5 = \binom{5}{0}2^5 + \binom{5}{1}2^4\left(-\frac{3}{2}x\right) + \binom{5}{2}2^3\left(-\frac{3}{2}x\right)^2 + \cdots$.
Carefully compute each coefficient to obtain terms in ascending powers of $x$.
walkthrough:
Apply the Binomial Theorem to expand $\left(2 - \frac{3}{2}x\right)^5$ up to the $x^2$ term:
$$\left(2 - \frac{3}{2}x\right)^5 = \binom{5}{0}(2)^5 + \binom{5}{1}(2)^4\left(-\frac{3}{2}x\right) + \binom{5}{2}(2)^3\left(-\frac{3}{2}x\right)^2 + \cdots$$

Calculate the numerical coefficients for each of the first three terms:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Term 1: } & 1 \times 32 = 32 \\ \text{Term 2: } & 5 \times 16 \times \left(-\frac{3}{2}x\right) = -120x \\ \text{Term 3: } & 10 \times 8 \times \left(\frac{9}{4}x^2\right) = 180x^2 \end{aligned}$$

Combine the simplified terms in ascending powers of $x$:
$$32 - 120x + 180x^2$$

hints: Substitute $x = 0.01$ into $32 - 120x + 180x^2$ to calculate the approximation.
walkthrough:
Equate $2 - \frac{3}{2}x$ to $1.985$ to determine the suitable value of $x$:
$$2 - \frac{3}{2}x = 1.985 \implies \frac{3}{2}x = 0.015 \implies x = 0.01$$

Substitute $x = 0.01$ into the quadratic polynomial from part (a):
$$1.985^5 \approx 32 - 120(0.01) + 180(0.01)^2$$
